newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent edges up, cautious correction seen.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent edges up, cautious correction seen.

text.p: Brent crude futures prices were higher in late trading in Asia on Thursday as some players bought back short position, but volume was slight.
July last traded on SIMEX at $17.48 per barrel, up 13 cents from London where prices fell overnight 15 to settle at $17.35, just three cents above the intraday low and fresh 13-month low.
The move higher was supported by a modest rise on ACCESS trading of NYMEX crudes in Asia. July was last traded at $18.64, up 11 cents from New York.
Brokers said the SIMEX mood remained cautious after two sessions of fresh 13-month lows and it would let London take the initiative on setting direction.
However, they said a stronger upward correction might be seen Thursday and Friday compared with the modest effort Wednesday, as players cut back short positions ahead of the weekend.
The low Brent price and steep contango is attracting West African cargoes east, which might help tighten the Atlantic Basin market and so offer some fundamental support to Brent.
